JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioners in the nutshell is that on 24.11.2023 at about 11.55 p.m, the deceased was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-17-HK-7131 along with his friend Thippeswamy from Annapura towards Davanagere on NH-48 road, in slowly by observing all the traffic rules and regulations and when he reached near Mallashettiahlli vilalge, towards Chitradurga - Davanagere NH-48 road, Davanagere District, at that time the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-25- MB-1159 had driven the same in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and dashed to the rear side of the deceased's motorcycle and caused the accident.
Due to the terrific impact the deceased fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over his body and succumbed to the fatal injuries on the spot.
Postmortem was conducted at General Hospital, Chigateri and corpse was handed over to the family members, who conducted funeral and other ceremonies by spending substantial amount.
It is contended that the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the driver of car and as such both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, prayed to allow the petition.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1.
Respondent No.1 appeared through his counsel by filing written statement rather objections to the main petition contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.

This respondent has denied that the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car but contended that the deceased himself is the sole responsible for the accident.
The respondent No.1 admitted that he is the RC owner of the car and was duly insured with the 2 nd respondent and same was in force as on the date of accident.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. After service of notice, the respondent No.2 appeared before the Court by filing written statement rather objections to the petition contending that the petition is not maintainable either law or on facts.
The respondent No.2 admitting the issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of car bearing Reg.No.KA-25-MB-1159.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
Non -compliance of section's 134(c) and 158(6), 159 of MV Act is pleaded.

This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode Parwathamma vs Mahendra Horkeri on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106285160/
2 and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Negligence on the part of the driver of its insured vehicle is denied by this respondent.

Per contra it is alleged that the deceased who was riding the motorcycle without having a proper lookout at the vehicular movement on the road and the deceased was solely responsible for the occurrence of the accident.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the insured vehicle did not possess valid & effective DL.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.
In fact deceased was also not wearing helmet and also not possessing valid DL at the time of alleged accident
. On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the 2nd respondent is not liable to indemnify him.

The respondent denied the relationship of the petitioners No.1(a) to (c) and further they are the major brothers and sisters of the deceased, residing separately and having their own independent income, they were not depending on the deceased income.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. It is pertinent to note that, at the first instance the petitioner by name Parvathamma (deceased mother) has filed this petition against the respondents for seeking compensation for the death of his son in RTA that occurred on 24.11.2023.
Further unfortunately, the petitioner i.e., Parvathamma expired on 16.09.2024 i.e., during the pendency of the petition.
Hence her Legal representatives was brought on record as petitioners No.1(a) to (c) vide orders dated 02.12.2024.
Thereafter the respondent No.2 filed written statement alleging that the LR's of deceased petitioners are not the legal heirs of the deceased, but they have not dependents of the deceased income.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased ?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 24.11.2023 at about 11.55 p.m.,
near Mallashettahalli Village, towards Chitradurga - Davanagere NH-48 road,
Davanagere District, due to actionable negligence of the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-25-MB- 1159 ?
3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation ?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
4) What order or award ?
7.
The Petitioner No.1(b) examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's .
P1 to 16were marked on behalf of the petitioners.

On the other hand the respondent No.2 examined its Legal Executive as RW.1.
Parwathamma vs Mahendra Horkeri on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106285160/
3 8.
Arguments were addressed on both sides.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

My answers to the above issues are as follows :-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per final order  for the following :
 REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.2 : The occurrence of the accident on the relevant date, time and place is not in dispute.
The parties are also not at variance with regard to the factum of the death of the deceased due to the injuries sustained in the said accident.
The conflict is with respect to actionable negligence.
The petitioners plead that the accident was caused due to the sole negligence of the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-25-MB-1159.
Whereas the insurance company contends that the accident in question occurred because of negligence of the deceased.

10. From the evidence on record it can be seen that after the receipt of complaint lodged by brother of deceased, Police registered a case against the driver of car in Crime No.416/2023 and after due investigation filed charge sheet against him for the offences punishable u/s 279, 338 & 304(A) of IPC.
The IMV report goes to show that at the time of inspection both the vehicles involved in the accident had sustained damages as detailed out in the said report.
Be that as it may, the IMV inspector has mentioned that he tested both the vehicles on road and found that their brake systems were in order.
He has thereby opined that the accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the above said vehicles.
Therefore the car driver did not have sufficient cause to cause the accident.
The fact that yet he went and dashed against the deceased's vehicle to rear side leads to drawing of an inference that he was driving his vehicle rashly and negligently.
11. The respondents who denied the cause of accident, has not let in any cogent evidence to prove its defence or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioners.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of law.
Further the respondents did not make any attempt to examine the driver of offending vehicle, who is the best witness to depose about the cause of accident.
There is no explanation to that effect.
Non- examination of driver of offending vehicle is fatal to the defence of Respondents.
Hence its contention that there was no negligence on the part of driver of car has to be disbelieved.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the negligence of the driver of the car.
As such, I answer issue No.2 in the Affirmative.

12. ISSUE NO.1 and 3 : Since these issues are interlinked with each other, and they form part of the same transaction they are taken up together for common discussion to avoid the repetition of facts.

4 13.

The LR's of petitioners No.1(a) to (c) claim that at the first instance the deceased petitioner i.e.,
Parvathamma has filed petition for the death of her son by name Dayananda. K.B
in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 24.11.2023
. The petition is filed on 22.12.2023.

Further it is pertinent to note that during the pendency of the petition i.e., on 13.11.2024 the counsel for petitioner filed memo and produced death extract stating that the petitioner by name Parvathamma was died on 16.09.2024.

As per the order dated.13.11.2024, this Court allowed the application and permitted to come on record as LR's of deceased petitioner (Parvathamma).
14.

It is alleged that after amendment of the petition, the LR.No.1(b) himself examined as PW.1 and stated that petitioners No.1(a) to (c) are the children of the deceased petitioner (Parvathamma) and brother and sister of the deceased Dayananda.
K.B. To prove the same, petitioner No.(b) filed affidavit in lieu of his chief-examination and deposed about the above relationship.
The Aadhar cards of deceased, deceased petitioner No.1, LR's of petitioner No.1(a) to (c) are marked at Ex's.P.11 to 15 and contents of the police papers do fortify the said fact.
Further the PW.1 has also produced Ex.P.9 and 10 being the death certificate of deceased Dayananda and petitioner No.1 who is none other than the mother of the deceased.
On perusal of Ex.P.10 it is clear that during the pendency of the petition the mother of the deceased / petitioner No.1 died on 16.09.2024.
It is vociferously contended by respondent No.2 that petitioners No.1(a) to (c) are not dependents of the deceased as such they are not entitled for any claim under the dependent head.
15. The respondent No.2 counsel filed written arguments contended

that the petitioner No.1(a) to (c)
are major brothers and sister of the deceased, they are married and residing separately.

The petitioners are not eligible to claim compensation as they are not Class-I Leal Heirs, they are majors,
residing separately and they are having their own independent income and not depending on the alleged deceased in any manner.
16.
It is well settled that dependency must be established in order to claim compensation.
However during the course of his cross-examination PW.1 admitted that he and other petitioners are residing with separately and they are all married.
Further he admitted that the deceased K.B. Dayananda was married and divorced and she was residing separately.

Further when its comes to the dependency of the petitioners No.1(a) to (c), it is relevant to note that the petitioner No.1(a) and (b) are the brothers and petitioner No.1(c) is the married sister of the deceased.
Petitioners No.1(a) to (c) have attained majority.

Added more there is nothing placed on record before the court that the petitoners No.1(a) to (c) was the dependent of the earning of the deceased when such being the case they cannot be considered as a dependent on the deceased.
In this view of matter petitioners No.1(a) to 9(c) cannot be said to be dependents on the earnings of their deceased brother.

Since the evidence led by PW.1 is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, I hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.

17. The learned counsel for petitioners No.1(a) to (c) relied on the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA.No.101120/2023 in the case of United India Ins.Co.Ltd v/s Sri. Umaji and another.

5 18.

Further respondent No.2 relied on the decision reported in ILR 2008 KAR 1561, in the case of M/s Oriental Ins.Co.Ltd V/s Shivamma and others, wherein it is held that, Finding of the Tribunal awarding compensation under the head "Loss of Dependency" - Legality of - HELD, If the claimants were not dependent on the income of the deceased, compensation under the head "Loss of dependency" cannot be granted.

entities.text: M/s Oriental Ins.Co.Ltd V/s Shivamma and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At the best in such circumstances, a nominal sum as compensation towards "loss of estate" can be granted by applying an appropriate multiplier - Further Held, Where the claimants who are dependents of deceased, claim loss of dependency and where the claimants who are not the dependents of the deceased claim only loss to estate - ON FACTS, HELD, The claimants were not dependents on the income of the deceased - Therefore, the claimants are entitled to compensation for loss of estate.

19. The respondent No.2 also relied on the decision reported in ILR 2004 KAR 3268, in the case of A. Manavalagan V/s A. Krishnamurthy and others, wherein it is held that :
(A) Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 - Section 173(1) -
Compensation - Method of computation of - Held - Law contemplates two categories of damages on the death of a person -

entities.text: A. Manavalagan V/s A. Krishnamurthy and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The first is the pecuniary loss sustained by the dependent members of his family -
The second is the loss caused to the estate of the deceased -
In the first category, the action is brought by the legal representatives, as trustees for the dependents beneficially entitled -
In the second category, the action is brought by the legal representatives, on behalf of the estate of the deceased and the compensation when recovered, forms part of the assets of the estate.

(B) Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 - Section 168 - Powers of the Tribunal under - Held - Tribunal can specify the persons to whom compensation should be paid and also specify how it should be distributed in the case of first category - But in the case second category, no such adjustments or alteration of shares is permissible and the entire amount has to be awarded to the benefit of the estate.
(C) Motor vehicles Act, 1988- Section 168, 173 claim by the defendants - Basis for award of compensation - Held -

The basis for award of compensation is the loss of dependency, that is loss of what was contributed by the deceased to such claimants, A conventional amount is awarded towards loss of expectation of life, under the head of loss to estate.
(D) Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 - Sections 168, 173 Claim by the Legal Representatives - Basis for award of compensation - Held -
The basis for award of compensation is the loss to the estate, that is the loss of saving by the deceased.
A conventional sum for loss of expectation of life added.
(E) Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 - Sections 168, 173 if the claimant legal heir is not a dependent what would be the position - Held -
Obviously, the question of awarding any amount under the head of loss of dependency would not arise, as there was no financial dependency.

Parwathamma vs Mahendra Horkeri on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106285160/
6 20.

In this regard reliance is placed on the decision reported in 2004 (5) KAR. L. J. 321 (DB),
wherein it is held that "Question of awarding compensation under the head 'loss of dependency'
would not arise in the absence of financial dependency of the claimant on the income of the deceased.
Claim petition to be treated as one on behalf of estate of the deceased and compensation received by the claimant forms part of that estate.

Basis for award of compensation is 'loss of estate';
to be determined by capitalization method involving ascertaining multiplicand and multiplying it by appropriate multiplier.
Annual savings of the deceased constitutes multiplicand.
The quantum of savings can be taken as one- fourth which will apply where the family consists of non-dependent spouse / children / parents.
Where the claimants are the non-dependent brothers / sisters claiming on behalf of the estate, the savings can be taken as 15% of the income.

The above percentages of course are subject to any specific evidence to the contrary led by the claimants".
21.

Reliance is also placed on the decision reported in ILR 2008 KAR 1561 wherein it is held that "If claimants were not dependent on the income of the deceased, compensation under the head 'loss of dependency' cannot be granted.
At best in such circumstances, a nominal sum as compensation towards 'loss of estate' can be granted by applying an appropriate multiplier".
The ratio deducible from the decisions supra is aptly applicable to the facts of the case on hand.
In the absence of financial dependency of the claimants on the deceased they are only entitled to compensation under the head "Loss of estate'.
22. Thus as per the own admission of PW.1 the claimants were not financially dependent on the deceased.
Accordingly as the above decisions referred supra, the petitioners are not entitled to receive any compensation under the head 'Loss of dependency'.

However keeping in view the fact that the petitioners are legal representatives of the deceased they are entitled to 'loss of estate'.
23.
Taking into consideration the age of the deceased as indicated in the PM report i.e., 49 years the appropriate multiplier applicable as per Sarla Verma's case is '13'.

Though petitioners claimed that deceased was an agriculturist by profession and thereby he was earning Rs.40,000/- p.m., they have not produced any documentary proof before the Court to substantiate the same.
24. In the absence of proof, it is the practice of the Courts to take the notional income.

Admittedly,
the accident is of the year 2023.

Hence the notional income of the deceased is taken at Rs.16,000/-
p.m.
After deduction of 3/4th towards his living and personal expenses of the deceased, the savings of the deceased would be Rs.4,000/- p.m. (Rs.48,000/- per annum) (16,000-12,000).
Hence the petitioners are entitled to Rs.6,24,000/- (4,000 X 12 X 13) towards 'Loss of estate'.

In addition to this the claimants are entitled to Rs.10,000/- towards the 'loss of 'loss of expectation of life' and Rs.15,000/- towards 'Funeral expenses'.
25.

The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Loss of dependency : - Nil - 2 Loss of Estate : 6,24,000-00 3 Loss of expectation : 10,000-00 of life.
 4

Funeral Expenses : 15,000-00 Parwathamma vs Mahendra Horkeri on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106285160/
7
Further it is pertinent to note that the petitioners have not impleaded the wife of the deceased by name Smt. K.G. Nethra as she is the Class - I legal heirs of the deceased.
The PW.1 has admitted in his cross examination that the deceased was married and divorced and his wife is residing separately.
Further it is noteworthy to state that deceased wife is alive, the petitioners has not produced any documentary proof with regard to Divorce.
Further on perusal of records, the xerox copy of judgment in MFA.10287/2011 is available on records.
On perusal of Judgment in MFA.No.10287/2011 of Honble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru dated.05.09.2012.
The said MFA is filed by the deceased / K.B. Dayanand against his wife by name Smt. K.G. Nethra.

Further this MFA is filed u/s 19(1) of Family Court Act r/w Sec.28 of Hindu Marriage Act, against the Judgment and Decree dated.19.09.2011 passed in M.C.No.29/2011 on the file of Family Court,
Davanagere, Allowing the petition filed u/s 13(1)(1-A) of Hindu Marriage Act for Divorce.
Further Honble High Court of Karnataka ordered as : "Learned Counsel for the appellant files a memo for withdrawal of appeal.
It is stated that the appellant has paid a sum of Rs.16,50,000/- to the respondent by way of final settlement and therefore, seeks permission to withdraw the appeal.
In view of the above, appeal is dismissed as withdrawn".
27. Further the petitioners have produced the G-Tree dated.04.11.2024 and same is marked at Ex.P.8, wherein the deceased wife name is shown as Smt. K.G.Netra.
Hence it is clearls that wife of the deceased is alive and she is the Class I legal heir of deceased.
But as per the Judgment in MFA.No.10287/2011 of Honble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru dated.05.09.2012, the wife of deceased has received amount towards final settlement.
Hence she is not entitled any compensation in this petition.
28. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY :
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
29. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of car bearing Reg.No.KA-25-MB-1159 and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners No.1(a) to (c) together with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within two months from the date of this order.

Hence issue No.1 & 3 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
30.
ISSUE NO.4 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :

8 ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioners No.1(a) to (c) are entitled for compensation of Rs.6,49,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - (Since Dead by LR's) Petitioner No.1(a)- 34% Petitioner No.1(b)-
33% Petitioner No.1(c)- 33%

After deposit of compensation amount the office is directed to release the entire share with interest of the petitioner No.1(a) to (c)
through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.

The fact that yet he went and dashed against the deceased's vehicle to rear side leads to drawing of an inference that he was driving his vehicle rashly and negligently.
11. The respondents who denied the cause of accident, has not let in any cogent evidence to prove its defence or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioners.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of law.
Further the respondents did not make any attempt to examine the driver of offending vehicle, who is the best witness to depose about the cause of accident.
There is no explanation to that effect.
Non- examination of driver of offending vehicle is fatal to the defence of Respondents.
Hence its contention that there was no negligence on the part of driver of car has to be disbelieved.
It is vociferously contended by respondent No.2 that petitioners No.1(a) to (c) are not dependents of the deceased as such they are not entitled for any claim under the dependent head.
that the petitioner No.1(a) to (c)
are major brothers and sister of the deceased, they are married and residing separately.
The petitioners are not eligible to claim compensation as they are not Class-I Leal Heirs, they are majors,
residing separately and they are having their own independent income and not depending on the alleged deceased in any manner.
16.
It is well settled that dependency must be established in order to claim compensation.
Further when its comes to the dependency of the petitioners No.1(a) to (c), it is relevant to note that the petitioner No.1(a) and (b) are the brothers and petitioner No.1(c) is the married sister of the deceased.
Added more there is nothing placed on record before the court that the petitoners No.1(a) to (c) was the dependent of the earning of the deceased when such being the case they cannot be considered as a dependent on the deceased.
In this view of matter petitioners No.1(a) to 9(c) cannot be said to be dependents on the earnings of their deceased brother.
Since the evidence led by PW.1 is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, I hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.
The basis for award of compensation is the loss to the estate, that is the loss of saving by the deceased.
Obviously, the question of awarding any amount under the head of loss of dependency would not arise, as there was no financial dependency.

The quantum of savings can be taken as one- fourth which will apply where the family consists of non-dependent spouse / children / parents.
Hence it is clearls that wife of the deceased is alive and she is the Class I legal heir of deceased.
Hence she is not entitled any compensation in this petition.
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.

8 ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioners No.1(a) to (c) are entitled for compensation of Rs.6,49,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.
On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Petitioner No.1 - (Since Dead by LR's) Petitioner No.1(a)- 34% Petitioner No.1(b)-
33% Petitioner No.1(c)- 33%
After deposit of compensation amount the office is directed to release the entire share with interest of the petitioner No.1(a) to (c)
through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
